title: Building Strong & Independent Men: Rise of the Natural Übermensch (Anti-Fragility)
summary: An Educated Barbarian lecture on Nietzsche's Beyond Good and Evil, focused on independence as the basis of the superior man and the new philosophers he calls tempters. NH contrasts them with modern free spirits, whom he identifies with progressives chained to morality, and argues that avoiding suffering and choosing comfort lead to stagnation.
claims: Independence is the core of Nietzsche's superior man: submit yourself to tests judged only by yourself, in solitude, without the carrot or the stick
Most men need external motivation, either reward or force; self-judged tests eliminate about 99% of people because any failure can only be blamed on yourself
To conserve oneself means not depending on others financially, emotionally or for acceptance; not becoming a hermit, but developing alone and re-entering the group as a valuable asset
Every person is both a prison and a recess: others constrain you through shame and also offer excuses and diversions, and both block independence
The weak man is the miser and the egoist because he has nothing to spare; the strong man has plenty to spare and tends toward generosity
Freedom for its own sake is destruction, like Icarus; build solitude in order to reach independence, not the reverse, because being useful is what makes men happiest
Slavery means someone else decides when and for what you expend your strength; independence means you choose
Anyone who abstracts ideas to understand the world is a philosopher; Nietzsche's tempters stay a puzzle and refuse to dumb knowledge down for the masses
Subjectivity should be embraced, not hidden behind claims of objectivity; a human without subjectivity is a non-being
The common good is a social consensus used to shame individuals who emancipate themselves back into the herd
Taboos are chains we uphold ourselves; the ability to slay the sacred cow separates the free man from the unfree
Modern self-proclaimed free spirits, whom he identifies as progressives, are chained to democratic and moral ideas, police speech and blame society for all misery
Rejecting personal responsibility is the clearest sign someone is not independent; the free man thrives on responsibility
Putting security and comfort above freedom erodes freedom, even though security and comfort come from freedom and responsibility
His pet theory: humans are declining physically, intellectually and morally because they try to exit nature and abolish suffering, and evolution only happens within nature
Refusing to suffer leads to stagnation; beware people who try to keep you from suffering for your own good, because they are removing their own discomfort
Comfort corrodes the soul; hyper-privileged people with no problems cannot grow and invent problems to solve
Nietzsche held that oppression makes groups stronger; pain can lift you up or drag you down, but removing it entirely causes stagnation
The new philosopher may wear a social mask to fit in, but must never let the mask become his true identity
Nietzsche was not a moral relativist: morals should be questioned and their origins traced, not abolished; the title Beyond Good and Evil was partly trolling
You cannot implant an idea that a person cannot tie to their own will to power; manipulation mostly works by offering comfortable excuses
He believes Nietzsche was not anti-religion but disgusted with the state of religion in his time
